bromsgrove.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Bromsgrove
s1loc: Bromsgrove has a busy charitable scene anchored by Primrose Hospice and Family Support Centre, whose High Street shop helps fund care for people living with life-limiting illness. The Basement Project supports young people up to 25 and runs a foodbank in the town centre, while a volunteer-run foodbank serves Catshill and a community larder operates in nearby Alvechurch. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks back much of this work, and the Bromsgrove and Redditch Methodist Circuit coordinates local foodbank collections across the district.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops on the High Street and central buying behind them, alongside the Primrose Hospice charity shops. Set against that are small community groups, the Catshill and Alvechurch projects, pantries and volunteer-run efforts working on a shoestring across Sidemoor, Charford and the surrounding villages. We are set up to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest groups.

Beyond food support, Bromsgrove draws on the wider Worcestershire Hospices Lottery, which funds Acorns Children's Hospice, St Richard's Hospice and Primrose Hospice between them. Charity shops line the High Street and Worcester Road, raising over a quarter of the hospice's yearly running costs, and mutual-aid and church groups keep collection points across Aston Fields, Lickey End and Stoke Prior. Volunteer drivers, sorters and shop teams give their time across these neighbourhoods, and kit that looks the part helps every one of them turn out with pride.

stratford-upon-avon.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Stratford-upon-Avon
s1loc: Stratford-upon-Avon Foodbank, part of the nationwide Trussell network, works to relieve poverty across the town and surrounding villages with emergency food and practical help given with dignity. It is backed by a strong team of more than 150 volunteers who collect donations from supermarkets, sort stock in the warehouse and staff food drives. The Holy Trinity Church and other congregations host collection points, and the big food-redistribution networks keep the warehouse supplied through the year.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops on Wood Street and the Alcester Road with central buying behind them, including the Myton Hospices and Shakespeare Hospice shops and a British Heart Foundation shop. Set against that are small community groups, pantries and volunteer-run projects on a shoestring across Shottery, Tiddington and Bishopton. We are set up to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest groups.

The Myton Hospices field almost a thousand volunteers across their shops and care, and the Shakespeare Hospice covers the wider district for collections from its Stratford base. Charity shops cluster around the town centre and the Maybird and Alcester Road parades, raising the funds that pay for end-of-life care. Volunteer drivers, befrienders, sorters and shop teams give their time across Clopton, Old Town and the riverside neighbourhoods, and dependable, smart kit helps each of them look the part at fetes, collections and the counter alike.

s1loc: Newark Foodbank, set up in 2012 and now a charity in its own right within the Trussell network, is run and staffed entirely by volunteers from Newark Community Support on Carter Gate, opening Tuesdays and Fridays. Beaumond House Hospice Care provides day hospice support and runs charity shops on Stodman Street and Robin Hood Walk. brentwood.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Brentwood

It is run by Doddinghurst Road Community Church in partnership with Brentwood Baptist Church, working with frontline care agencies to reach the most vulnerable.
